artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan aligning theory operator Unicode aliases with the Logos manual: curated glyph registry plus cross-theory printability test, bimodal and constitutive alias changes, jupyter notation-map sync, and a complete OPERATORS.md manual-symbol table.

user_decision.question: Should the Unicode alias U+2AAF for the relevance operator \preceq be retired, or kept despite failing the printability criterion this task introduces (carried by exactly 1 monospace font family) and despite the Logos manual independently using that glyph for duration ordering?
options: Retire it - remove the alias, keep \preceq as the sole spelling, consistent with the new printability criterion and with the already-unaliased \next/\prev/\CFBox/\CFDiamond precedent
Keep it - grandfather the glyph into the curated registry as a documented exception, preserving the existing user-facing spelling and its relevance-logic literature mnemonic
user_decision.recommended: Retire it - remove the alias, keep \preceq as the sole spelling, consistent with the new printability criterion and with the already-unaliased \next/\prev/\CFBox/\CFDiamond precedent
